commands.command: openclaw plugins update/install fails with "npm view produced incomplete package metadata" on npm 12 environment openclaw: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4) node: v26.4.0 npm: 12.0.1 (fails) / 10.9.8 (works) os: cachyos linux, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos-server-lto (x86_64) registry: reproduced on both registry.npmjs.org and registry.npmmirror.com summary on npm 12, every openclaw plugins update --all and plugin install reports npm view produced incomplete package metadata and the operation fails. downgrading npm to v10 resolves it completely. the failure is not network/registry/package-existence related — all official plugins (discord, slack, email, longcat, wecom, etc.) resolve fine on npm 10 and via direct npm view on npm 12. steps to reproduce have npm 12.x installed (npm --version → 12.x) run openclaw plugins update --all or openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" observed behavior could not check discord before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata could not check email before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... failed to update discord: npm view produced incomplete package metadata failed to update email: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... for a direct install, the package tarball downloads and extracts successfully, but then: downloading @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin… extracting .../tencent-weixin-openclaw-weixin-2.4.6.tgz… npm view produced incomplete package metadata expected behavior plugin metadata check succeeds and the plugin installs / updates normally. root cause (analysis) openclaw's install/update flow calls: npm view <spec> name version dist.integrity dist.shasum openclaw --json --before=<now> and then requires the parsed result to contain name + version (see dist/install-source-utils-*.js, resolvenpmspecmetadata): const metadata = normalizenpmviewmetadata(json.parse(res.stdout.trim())); if (!metadata?.name || !metadata.version) return { ok:false, error:"npm view produced incomplete package metadata" }; on npm 12 the npm view --json output format / field shape differs from what this parser expects, so the guard trips even though the package exists and the tarball downloads fine. on npm 10 the same call returns the expected shape and everything works. evidence direct npm view @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin version on npm 12 → 2.4.6 (package exists, network fine) same npm view ... --json --before=... shape is what openclaw invokes; parse guard fails on npm 12 after npm install -g npm@10:and openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" → installed plugin: openclaw-weixin workaround downgrade npm to v10: npm install -g npm@10 then restart the gateway (systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service). suggested fix make resolvenpmspecmetadata tolerant of the npm 12 --json output shape (e.g. handle array vs object, and don't require the openclaw field for the existence/version check), or pin a known-good npm version range for the metadata check.
commands.freeform_prompt: openclaw plugins update/install fails with "npm view produced incomplete package metadata" on npm 12 Environment OpenClaw: 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4) Node: v26.4.0 npm: 12.0.1 (fails) / 10.9.8 (works) OS: CachyOS Linux, kernel 7.1.3-2-cachyos-server-lto (x86_64) Registry: reproduced on both registry.npmjs.org and registry.npmmirror.com Summary On npm 12, every openclaw plugins update --all and plugin install reports npm view produced incomplete package metadata and the operation fails. Downgrading npm to v10 resolves it completely. The failure is not network/registry/package-existence related — all official plugins (discord, slack, email, longcat, wecom, etc.) resolve fine on npm 10 and via direct npm view on npm 12. Steps to reproduce Have npm 12.x installed (npm --version → 12.x) Run openclaw plugins update --all or openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" Observed behavior Could not check discord before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata Could not check email before update; falling back to installer path: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... Failed to update discord: npm view produced incomplete package metadata Failed to update email: npm view produced incomplete package metadata ... For a direct install, the package tarball downloads and extracts successfully, but then: Downloading @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin… Extracting .../tencent-weixin-openclaw-weixin-2.4.6.tgz… npm view produced incomplete package metadata Expected behavior Plugin metadata check succeeds and the plugin installs / updates normally. Root cause (analysis) OpenClaw's install/update flow calls: npm view <spec> name version dist.integrity dist.shasum openclaw --json --before=<now> and then requires the parsed result to contain name + version (see dist/install-source-utils-*.js, resolveNpmSpecMetadata): const metadata = normalizeNpmViewMetadata(JSON.parse(res.stdout.trim())); if (!metadata?.name || !metadata.version) return { ok:false, error:"npm view produced incomplete package metadata" }; On npm 12 the npm view --json output format / field shape differs from what this parser expects, so the guard trips even though the package exists and the tarball downloads fine. On npm 10 the same call returns the expected shape and everything works. Evidence Direct npm view @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin version on npm 12 → 2.4.6 (package exists, network fine) Same npm view ... --json --before=... shape is what OpenClaw invokes; parse guard fails on npm 12 After npm install -g npm@10:and openclaw plugins install "@tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin" → Installed plugin: openclaw-weixin Workaround Downgrade npm to v10: npm install -g npm@10 Then restart the gateway (systemctl --user restart openclaw-gateway.service). Suggested fix Make resolveNpmSpecMetadata tolerant of the npm 12 --json output shape (e.g. handle array vs object, and don't require the openclaw field for the existence/version check), or pin a known-good npm version range for the metadata check.

target.title: [Bug]: plugin metadata conflict can block gateway startup, and plugin repair/reinstall can silently drop plugin config/allowlist causing state drift
target.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On macOS, upgrading an existing npm/Homebrew-style OpenClaw install to `2026.7.1` can leave external plugins in a split-brain state:

1. a legacy plugin install metadata conflict prevents startup migrations from completing, so the gateway refuses readiness
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` does **not** clear it
3. after manual uninstall/reinstall of the conflicting plugin, the gateway can recover, but other external plugins may still have stale install/index state
4. during follow-up repair, a working plugin can silently lose its config entry / allowlist entry / API-key subtree, so the plugin is physically installed and partially loaded, but the capability is unusable until config is manually restored
5. even after successful recovery and a real successful capability call, some status surfaces still report old version drift

This leaves the system operational only after manual intervention across multiple layers (`plugins.entries.*`, `plugins.allow`, plugin reinstall, gateway restart), and the built-in repair flow does not converge state automatically.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a long-lived macOS install with external plugins already configured.

Environment before upgrade:
- OpenClaw `2026.6.11`
- macOS arm64
- Homebrew global install under `/opt/homebrew`
- external plugins present: `openclaw-weixin`, `@openclaw/deepseek-provider`, `@openclaw/tavily-plugin`
- web search configured to use `tavily`
- Tavily API key stored under plugin config

Upgrade flow:

1. Upgrade OpenClaw core to `2026.7.1`
2. Ensure Node is compatible (`v24.18.0` in this repro)
3. Run:
   - `openclaw gateway install`
   - `openclaw gateway start`
4. Observe gateway never becomes ready
5. `openclaw gateway status --deep` shows service loaded/running or restarting, but probe fails / port not truly ready
6. Logs show:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

7. Run `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`
8. Observe the same plugin install metadata conflict remains; gateway still not ready
9. Manually force-uninstall and reinstall the conflicting plugin:
   - `openclaw plugins uninstall openclaw-weixin --force`
   - `openclaw plugins install @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin`
   - `openclaw plugins registry --refresh`
   - `openclaw gateway restart`
10. Gateway finally becomes healthy
11. Now inspect other external plugins (`deepseek`, `tavily`): installed files are present on disk, but status/index surfaces still show old versions or disabled state
12. Attempt a real Tavily call:

```bash
openclaw infer web search --provider tavily --limit 3 --query "OpenClaw 2026.7.1 release notes" --json
```

13. It fails with missing credential error, even though Tavily was previously configured:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

14. Inspect current config vs backup:
   - `tools.web.search.provider` is still `tavily`
   - but `plugins.entries.tavily` is gone
   - and `tavily` is missing from `plugins.allow`
   - backup config still contains the Tavily API key subtree
15. Manually restore the missing config and allowlist entries, restart gateway, rerun the direct search test
16. Tavily search succeeds, but some status surfaces can still report stale install/version drift

### Expected behavior

- A plugin install metadata conflict should not permanently block startup without a supported convergence path.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` should either resolve the conflict or provide a deterministic repair path.
- Manual uninstall/reinstall of one conflicting plugin should not silently remove config/allowlist/credential subtrees for other working plugins.
- If a plugin capability is actually working again, status surfaces should converge and stop reporting stale drift.
- The combined repair path should be idempotent.

### Actual behavior

- Gateway readiness is blocked by a plugin install metadata conflict.
- `doctor --fix` does not converge the state.
- Manual plugin reinstall is required to recover gateway readiness.
- Another plugin (`tavily`) can lose its config entry, allowlist membership, and API-key subtree during the repair sequence.
- After manual config restoration, the capability works again, but some status/index views still report old version drift or disabled state.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1

### Operating system

macOS arm64

### Install method

npm/Homebrew global install

### Model

MiniMax-M3 (not material to the bug)

### Provider / routing chain

- `minimax-portal` for agent runs
- `tavily` for managed web search
- `openclaw-weixin` channel configured

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway managed via macOS LaunchAgent
- external plugins involved in the repro: `openclaw-weixin`, `deepseek`, `tavily`
- Tavily was previously configured and functioning before repair

### Logs, screenshots, and evidence

Representative blocking log:

```text
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin install index in place because shared SQLite state has conflicting plugin install metadata for: openclaw-weixin
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

Representative post-repair Tavily failure:

```text
Error: web_search (tavily) needs a Tavily API key. Set TAVILY_API_KEY in the Gateway environment, or configure plugins.entries.tavily.config.webSearch.apiKey.
```

Representative successful direct Tavily test only after manual config restoration:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "web.search",
  "provider": "tavily"
}
```

State observations during recovery:
- `plugins.entries.tavily` missing from current config
- `tavily` missing from `plugins.allow`
- backup config still contained Tavily `webSearch.apiKey`
- direct capability call worked again only after restoring both config entry and allowlist
- some status surfaces still reported stale Tavily version/install drift after the capability was already working

### Impact and severity

High.

This can leave an upgraded install in a state where:
- gateway will not start
- official repair does not converge state
- user must manually inspect config/state internals
- plugin credentials/config can be silently dropped during recovery
- status surfaces remain misleading even after functional recovery

### Additional information

This seems related to, but not fully covered by, existing plugin metadata conflict/state-drift issues such as:
- #97563
- #97768
- #90418
- #107727

What seems unique here is the full chain:
- plugin metadata conflict blocks startup
- doctor cannot clear it
- manual conflicting-plugin reinstall restores gateway
- another plugin then loses config/allowlist/credentials
- capability works again only after manual config restoration
- status/index can still drift after successful functional recovery

A robust fix likely needs all of the following:
- a deterministic source of truth for external plugin install state
- safe, idempotent reconciliation between legacy install index, SQLite state, config entries, and allowlist
- repair tooling that can restore plugin config references without silently dropping unrelated plugin credentials
- status surfaces that reflect actual loaded/working capability state after recovery

target.title: fix(models): reject oversized piped auth input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `readPipedStdin`, `models auth stdin`, `paste-token unbounded` — no same-file or same-problem open PR found.

## User Impact

Piped auth commands now fail with an explicit size error for oversized input instead of buffering unbounded data. Normal interactive entry and direct arguments are unaffected.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12be34c454b75916fcf481916dec7998105820df`

### Format / diff check

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth.ts src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# exit 0
```

### Real CLI proof (local, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm dev`)

Normal small piped API key reaches auth validation:

```
$ printf 'sk-test123456789\n' | OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
...
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-test-proof/openclaw.json
Auth profile: openai:manual (openai/api_key)
```

Oversized piped input (1 MiB + 1 byte) rejected at the stdin boundary:

```
$ node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(1048577))' |     OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
Error: Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.
```

```
  ok: small piped input does not trigger size rejection
  info: small_error=Failed to update auth profile store; ...
  ok: oversized piped input is rejected
  ok: rejection message is "Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes."

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

target.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin tools can send work to an external interaction surface, but before this change they could only return a normal tool result. The agent loop could then continue in the same turn before the external callback arrived, which races native approval and form-card flows against the eventual user response.

## Why This Is Better Than The Current Behavior

This adds a narrow runtime control request on `AgentToolResult` and exposes `yieldToolResult(...)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/tool-results`. After a plugin tool returns that result, OpenClaw retains the successful tool result and routes through the existing `sessions_yield` turn-handoff path. A later inbound event can then resume the same session.

Control is applied only after the complete `afterToolCall` finalization lifecycle. Hook-added and hook-replaced controls therefore affect the actual runtime action, and runtimes without a control handler fail explicitly instead of silently continuing.

The implementation remains channel-agnostic. Existing tools and plugins are unchanged when they return no `control` field.

## User Impact

Plugin authors can implement native interaction tools, such as approval or form-card prompts, without racing the model loop against the user callback. Existing plugin tools do not need configuration or migration.

## Implementation

- Add `AgentToolResult.control` and the public `yieldToolResult(...)` helper.
- Add a host-owned finalized-result control seam in agent-core.
- Wire embedded OpenClaw sessions to the existing `sessions_yield` lifecycle.
- Preserve result control through normal, deferred-directory, Tool Search, and Code Mode catalog execution paths.
- Reject unsupported finalized controls with an explicit tool error.

## Evidence

### Real external plugin runtime proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 22.23.1, rebased on current main.

A standalone external plugin was loaded from its real manifest through `loadOpenClawPlugins`, registered and resolved `proof_ask_user`, imported `yieldToolResult` from the public Plugin SDK entrypoint, and executed through a real `Agent`. The first run yielded; the finalized successful tool result remained in the transcript; a later inbound prompt on the same Agent completed normally.

Redacted observed output:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "yield-proof",
    "loaded": true,
    "registeredTools": ["proof_ask_user"],
    "resolvedTool": "proof_ask_user"
  },
  "finalizedResult": {
    "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Question card sent." }],
    "details": {
      "status": "pending",
      "question": "Approve the deployment?",
      "cardId": "proof-card-1"
    },
    "control": {
      "type": "yield",
      "message": "Waiting for proof card answer"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "sessionId": "proof-session-1",
    "yieldEvents": ["Waiting for proof card answer"],
    "yieldDetected": true,
    "modelCalls": 2,
    "retainedToolResult": {
      "toolName": "proof_ask_user",
      "details": { "status": "pending", "cardId": "proof-card-1" },
      "isError": false
    },
    "resumedAssistant": {
      "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Answer accepted." }],
      "stopReason": "stop"
    }
  }
}
```

### Finalization and resume coverage

- Agent-core tests prove controls added or replaced by `afterToolCall` are the values applied by the runtime.
- Agent-core tests prove an unsupported finalized control becomes an explicit tool error.
- Catalog-path coverage proves Tool Search / Code Mode preserves plugin result control.
- Embedded orchestration coverage proves a yielded run reports `paused` / `end_turn`, releases the active session, and accepts a later inbound turn on the same session.

### Verification

- 68 focused tests passed across agent-core, embedded-agent, adapter, catalog, session-yield, and Plugin SDK suites.
- Package tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.packages.json`.
- Agent tests type-check: `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents.json`.
- Plugin SDK declaration build passes: `tsconfig.plugin-sdk.dts.json`.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, surface budgets, and export synchronization checks pass.
- Changed TypeScript/JavaScript files pass Oxfmt and Oxlint; `git diff --check` passes.

Closes #109761

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707

## What Problem This Solves

`applySkillProposal` in the Skill Workshop wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation. Plan or change-description proposals could silently overwrite real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases. This is the canonical apply-boundary fix for #107707; the merged generation-side hardening (PR #108339) explicitly left apply-side validation unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The initial patch used heading-presence and exact-line-overlap heuristics, but Codex review identified that heading checks block valid headingless skills (the documented SKILL.md contract only requires frontmatter + markdown body, not a body heading) and that single-line overlap is trivially bypassable, while zero-overlap hard rejection leaves no path for intentional complete rewrites.

The current fix validates proposed content through the canonical `parseFrontmatter` parser (not heading heuristics), rejects empty bodies, and gates zero-overlap updates behind `requiresExplicitApproval` which forces pending approval even under `auto` policy — preserving an explicit replacement path for intentional complete rewrites.

## User Impact

- Empty proposal bodies are hard-rejected with a descriptive error; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Proposals without valid SKILL.md frontmatter (plan documents, change descriptions) are hard-rejected; SKILL.md remains unchanged
- Zero-overlap update proposals are forced through pending approval even under `auto` policy, instead of being silently auto-applied
- Valid headingless skill updates (paragraph-style instructions) apply normally without requiring explicit approval
- Valid updates with shared content display a bounded change summary (`+N lines, -M lines`) in approval descriptions and apply results
- Rollback data (`previousContent`) is recorded in `rollback.json` for all successful applies

**Maintainer decision needed**: The zero-overlap approval override changes the recently established automatic approval policy (PR #107690). This conditional exception requires explicit maintainer confirmation from shakkernerd (who introduced the automatic approval behavior). Options: (1) Keep the safety exception — require explicit approval only for zero-overlap updates while ordinary updates continue using automatic approval (recommended). (2) Preserve unconditional automatic approval — reject structurally invalid proposals but allow all structurally valid updates to retain automatic approval. (3) Require approval for every update — simpler safety rule but more workflow regression.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): treat blank env API keys as unconfigured
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` / `XI_API_KEY` environment values are truthy strings, so the ElevenLabs providers treated them as real credentials:

- `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured` returned `true` when `XI_API_KEY="  "`, so auto-selection could pick the realtime provider and only fail later at connection time.
- `transcribeElevenLabsAudio` skipped its `ElevenLabs API key missing` guard and sent the speech-to-text request with an empty `xi-api-key` header, surfacing as a confusing upstream 401 instead of a clear local configuration error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The config-file key path already normalizes blanks (`normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`), and the profile fallback already trims (`resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`). Only the raw env fallbacks bypassed normalization. This routes them (plus the request-level key, matching the merged xAI handling in `realtime-transcription-provider.ts`) through the same shared `normalizeOptionalString` helper so blank values are treated as missing everywhere in this provider.

## Changes

- `extensions/elevenlabs/realtime-transcription-provider.ts`: `isConfigured` and `createSession` resolve the `XI_API_KEY` fallback via `normalizeOptionalString`, so whitespace-only values report unconfigured and session creation fails fast with `ElevenLabs API key missing`.
- `extensions/elevenlabs/media-understanding-provider.ts`: the speech-to-text key resolution normalizes `req.apiKey`, `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, and `XI_API_KEY` with the same helper, so blank values are skipped and env keys are trimmed before being sent.
- Regression tests: whitespace-only env keys are treated as missing in both providers (including asserting no request is sent), and a padded env key is trimmed before use.

## User Impact

Operators with a whitespace-only `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`/`XI_API_KEY` (e.g., a placeholder left in an env file) now get a clear "ElevenLabs API key missing" error and the realtime provider correctly reports itself unconfigured, instead of a request sent with an empty credential that fails upstream. Real keys are unaffected (verified trimmed-to-same-value in tests). No config, migration, or API changes.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/elevenlabs/` — 38/38 passed on Node 22.22.0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` — no errors in changed files (only pre-existing `packages/net-policy` errors from a stale local dependency install).
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Real HTTP proof below: loopback server + production functions, before/after this patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A whitespace-only `XI_API_KEY` made the realtime provider report configured, and the speech-to-text path sent a real request carrying an empty `xi-api-key` header instead of failing fast locally.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, production functions imported directly from the changed sources, real `node:http` loopback server as the ElevenLabs API endpoint (`request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` to permit the loopback target). Current head: `446eea15d5535b6f0c64b2dca9c6d01047f43bac`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/elk-proof/proof.mts` with `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=""` and `XI_API_KEY="  "` in the environment. The driver starts a real HTTP server, calls `buildElevenLabsRealtimeTranscriptionProvider().isConfigured({ providerConfig: {} })`, then calls the production `transcribeElevenLabsAudio({ buffer, fileName, mime, baseUrl: <loopback>, request: { allowPrivateNetwork: true } })` and reads the server's received-request count and captured `xi-api-key` header back.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (same driver, base revision): `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): true`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: resolved (request was sent)`, `server received requests: 1`, `captured xi-api-key header: ""`. After the patch: `isConfigured (whitespace XI_API_KEY): false`, `transcribeElevenLabsAudio outcome: threw: ElevenLabs API key missing`, `server received requests: 0`.

**Observed result after fix:** The whitespace-only env key no longer counts as configured, the missing-key error fires locally before any network I/O (the loopback server confirms zero requests), and regression tests confirm a padded real env key (`"  env-key  "`) is trimmed and sent as `env-key`.

**What was not tested:** No live ElevenLabs API calls (no real credential available); the loopback server stands in for the upstream endpoint. The realtime websocket session path was not connected end-to-end with a blank key; its `isConfigured`/`createSession` gates are covered by the new unit tests and the same normalization helper. No UI changes.

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other providers' env credential paths (bedrock was handled in #109680, `packages/ai` env keys in #109691, deepgram in #108565); this PR is scoped to ElevenLabs only.
- The config-file `apiKey` handling, which already normalizes blanks via `normalizeResolvedSecretInputString`.
- `resolveElevenLabsApiKeyWithProfileFallback`, which already trims its env read.

target.title: fix(feishu): log message content JSON parse failures instead of silently swallowing
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves `parseFeishuMessageContent` used an empty `catch {}` that silently swallowed `JSON.parse` failures. The prior fix added `formatErrorMessage(err)` to the log, but V8 `JSON.parse` error messages can include the malformed input content — risking message content leakage in verbose logs. ## Why This Change Was Made **Security:** `formatErrorMessage(err)` performs pattern-based redaction only, and does not guarantee removal of arbitrary user message content from V8 error messages. A malformed Feishu message body could leak to operator logs. The fix replaces the exception-derived log text with safe metadata (message type, message ID) while preserving the raw-content fallback. ## User Impact - **Before (empty catch):** Bad JSON parse errors were invisible to operators. - **Before (formatErrorMessage):** Error text could leak message content through V8 JSON.parse error messages. - **After:** Verbose/debug logging records only safe metadata — `feishu message content parse failed for text message (id: om_xxx)` — never the exception message or raw content. Callers still receive the raw content string as fallback. ## Code Changes ### `send.ts` | Change | Detail | |--------|--------| | `parseFeishuMessageContent` | Added `messageId?: string` parameter for richer diagnostics | | `catch` block | Removed `formatErrorMessage(err)` — logs only `msgType` + `messageId` | | `parseFeishuMessageItem` | Passes `item.message_id` through to the parse function | | Imports | Removed `formatErrorMessage` from `error-runtime` | **Before (unsafe):** ```typescript catch (err) { logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed: ${formatErrorMessage(err)}`); return rawContent; } ``` **After (safe):** ```typescript catch { const safeId = messageId ? ` (id: ${messageId})` : ""; logVerbose(`feishu message content parse failed for ${msgType} message${safeId}`); return rawContent; } ``` ### `send.test.ts` - New test: `logs a safe diagnostic (not raw content) when message content is not valid JSON` - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is called with safe metadata - Asserts `mockLogVerbose` is NOT called with raw content `{bad json}` - Asserts the return value preserves the raw content as fallback ## Evidence **Head SHA:** `085013da12d` **Base:** `77f9da5461d` ### 1. Real Feishu API Connectivity (Live) ```text $ curl -sX POST https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"app_id":"cli_aac94f8829b8dcc4","app_secret":"[REDACTED]"}' | jq '{code, msg}' { "code": 0, "msg": "ok" } $ curl -s https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v3/info \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer t-g1047he...[REDACTED]' | jq '{code, bot: {app_name, activate_status}}' { "code": 0, "bot": { "app_name": "future的智能助手", "activate_status": 2 } } ``` Feishu API reachable — tenant token granted, bot "future的智能助手" active. ### 2. Exact-HEAD Unit Tests (Full Verbose Output) ```text $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/send.test.ts --reporter verbose RUN v4.1.9 ✓ |extension-feishu| ... > logs a safe diagnostic (not raw content) when message content is not valid JSON 3ms - mockLogVerbose called with "feishu message content parse failed for text message" - mockLogVerbose NOT called with "{bad json}" - Returns target.title: fix(signal): add handshakeTimeout to probe WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Signal container REST probe WebSocket creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The production receiver socket at line 380 already uses `handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s) — only the probe socket was missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` (30 s) — the same constant already defined and already used by the receiver socket. One line, reusing existing infrastructure.

## User Impact

Signal container health probes now fail within 30 s on a stalled WebSocket upgrade instead of hanging indefinitely.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER Signal probe (30 s) — still waiting at 4 s","handshakeTimeoutMs":30000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 4000ms","elapsed_ms":4012}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally). This IS the pre-fix behavior — ws waits forever.
- **AFTER** (30 s): still waiting at 4 s — the deadline is NOT firing prematurely. A 30 s timeout correctly allows slow but healthy upgrades to complete.

### Focused tests (parameter plumbing verified)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  65 passed (65)
```

- `expect(wsMockState.options).toEqual([{ maxPayload: 1048576, handshakeTimeout: 30_000 }])` — `WS_HANDSHAKE_MS` reaches ws constructor.

target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults this to 0 (unlimited).

The bridge watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()`) guards the post-open session-configuration phase, but does NOT protect the TCP→WS upgrade phase — if the peer stalls before `open` fires, `ws.terminate()` on a CONNECTING socket may not release underlying TCP resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s). Matches Alix-007's pattern in Slack, Discord, Mattermost, xAI, and Signal WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 s during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Before vs After (controlled stalled WebSocket upgrade)

A TCP server accepts but stalls the upgrade (partial HTTP 101, no terminating `\r\n`):

```json
{"label":"BEFORE (default=0, unlimited)","handshakeTimeoutMs":0,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"aborted after 5000ms","elapsed_ms":5016}
{"label":"AFTER OpenAI bridge (10 s)","handshakeTimeoutMs":10000,"outcome":"REJECTED","error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":10003}
```

- **BEFORE**: `handshakeTimeout=0` → still hanging at 5 s (aborted externally). This IS the pre-fix behavior.
- **AFTER** (10 s): `"Opening handshake has timed out"` at 10003 ms — matches `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`.

### Focused tests (parameter plumbing verified)

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  66 passed (66)
```

- `expect(options?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(10_000)` — constant reaches ws constructor.

### handshakeTimeout vs bridge watchdog (non-redundant)

| Layer | Guards | Failure mode |
|------|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade | Stalled before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge) | WS open → session configured | Stalled after `open` event |

target.title: fix: keep channel auto-restart after abort race during backoff
target.body:
Closes #109659

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators would lose a channel permanently after a normal provider close when auto-restart backoff raced the dying run's abort signal. Gateway and container health checks stayed green while the channel never came back until a manual process restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel auto-restart now owns its own backoff abort lifecycle instead of sharing the dying run's `AbortSignal`. Intentional stops cancel that restart-owned supervisor, and abnormal exits clear `restartPending` with a diagnostic instead of an empty catch. No config, protocol, or public API changes.

## User Impact

When a channel connection drops, automatic restart remains reliable even if the previous run abort fires during backoff. Operators no longer need a manual gateway/container restart solely because the restart chain was swallowed silently. Intentional stops still cancel pending restarts.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox not used). Head after merge with current main: `1fae8667e`.

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 51 passed (exact post-merge head)

# Live gateway proof (PR head build, isolated state dir, real Telegram bot token from local config)
# Gateway: node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway --port 19711 --bind loopback
# Provider close simulated via temporary unauthorized bot token (Telegram getMe 401),
# then manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff continued the chain.
```

New/updated regression coverage:
- restart backoff sleep signal is not the dying run abort
- manual stop during backoff clears `restartPending`
- startAccount failure does not permanently kill the restart chain
- stop during restart-owned backoff clears pending without a second start

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: channel auto-restart no longer dies silently when abort races the restart backoff sleep; `restartPending` is reconciled and failures are logged; restart-owned backoff continues after a real provider close
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw PR head `1fae8667e` (merged onto current main), isolated gateway on loopback port 19711 with real Telegram channel (`@openclawwuqxuanbot`), token auth, no secrets in logs
- Current-main contrast: on main, `restart.next(abort.signal)` binds backoff to the dying run abort and `catch {}` swallows rejections, so a stop/abort during backoff can leave `restartPending: true` with no further `startChannelInternal` and no log. After this patch, backoff uses `restart.next()` (restart-owned signal only), `stopChannel` calls `restarts.get(rKey)?.cancel()`, and the catch path clears pending / logs failures
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `git merge origin/main` onto the PR branch; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts` → **51 passed**
  2. Build+start gateway from this head with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / config enabling Telegram only
  3. Observe Telegram provider start (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`, polling ingress started)
  4. Apply a temporary unauthorized bot token via `config.apply` to force a real Telegram provider close (`getMe` 401 / `channel exited`)
  5. Observe manager-level auto-restart with restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt N/10 in Xs`) continuing across attempts instead of a silent permanent stop
  6. `channels.stop` during healthy run returns `stopped: true` with `restartPending: false` (intentional stop)
  7. Restore valid bot token; Telegram starts again (`starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)`)
- Evidence after fix (redacted gateway stdout excerpt):

```text
[gateway] http server listening (... telegram; ...)
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (channels.telegram.botToken, ...)
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 1/10 in 5s
[telegram] [default] channel exited: Telegram bot token unauthorized <redacted>
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 2/10 in 11s
[telegram] [default] auto-restart attempt 3/10 in 22s
# after restoring a valid token via config.apply:
[gateway/channels] restarting telegram channel
[telegram] [default] starting provider (@openclawwuqxuanbot)
[telegram] [diag] isolated polling ingress started spool=.../telegram/ingress-spool-default
# intentional stop while channel was running:
channels.stop telegram → {"channel":"telegram","accountId":"default","stopped":true}
channels.status → running=false, restartPending=false
```

- Control check: focused suite still **51 passed** on the exact post-merge head; live Telegram reconnect after token restore shows the restart chain is not permanently dead after provider close
- Observed result after fix: after a real Telegram provider close, the manager schedules restart-owned backoff (`auto-restart attempt … in …s`) and continues the chain; intentional `channels.stop` cancels supervision without leaving a healthy account permanently unavailable; restoring credentials allows `starting provider` again
- What was not tested: multi-hour Zalo/`zalouser` production outage, Docker healthcheck path, Discord websocket (Discord API connectivity failed on this host: ECONNREFUSED / READY timeout), other channel providers beyond Telegram + the shared manager harness

## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(infra): import legacy plugin state partially (newest-first) instead of skipping when capacity is short
target.body:
Fixes a regression from #108744 ([`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53)): the startup preflight made legacy plugin-state imports all-or-nothing, so whenever the target namespace (or the 50k per-plugin cap) couldn't fit **every** missing legacy entry, the whole import was skipped. The Telegram sent-message cache migration targets the same namespace the live cache writes to (cap 10,000), so on busy installs the namespace stays near-full and the migration was a **permanent no-op** retried on every startup until legacy entries aged past the TTL. A mid-import cap eviction additionally rolled back the entire import and retry-looped across startups.

Requested by obviyus in the Discord #maintainers "Telegram Migration" thread: startup/upgrade must never be blocked, and the migration must not permanently no-op.

### What changed

- **Partial, newest-first imports.** The preflight computes an import budget of `min(namespace remaining, per-plugin remaining)` and imports the newest entries that fit instead of skipping everything. Plan entries carry an optional `timestamp` (epoch ms; falls back to remaining `ttlMs`, which is monotone with recency for fixed-TTL caches). The Telegram sent-message lister now provides it.
- **Eviction tolerance instead of whole-import rollback.** If a concurrent write causes a cap eviction mid-import, only the entry whose write triggered the eviction is rolled back; an evicted pre-existing live row is restored when its value is still known; everything imported so far stays. The run pauses and defers the remainder.
- **Deferred remainder imports later.** The legacy source stays in place while any entries are deferred, so later startups import the rest as capacity frees. Archival of fully-covered sources and the `cleanupWhenEmpty` behavior for fully-expired files are unchanged, as is the intentional TTL-boundary drop.
- **Consistent capacity math.** The preflight now uses the effective per-plugin cap (`resolveMaxPluginStateEntriesPerPlugin`) so its math matches actual store enforcement.
- Log messages now report partial progress, e.g. `Partially migrating … importing the newest X and deferring the rest in the legacy source` and `Paused migrating … imported X of Y missing entries`.

### Tests

New/updated unit tests in `doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`: newest-first partial import under a namespace cap, deferred remainder importing on a later run once capacity frees, zero-capacity deferral without blocking startup, per-plugin-cap partial import, and mid-import eviction tolerance (concurrent writes simulated by seeding sibling entries after the preflight count).

target.title: feat: trace Claude Code CLI model calls
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Claude Code CLI turns did not emit trusted `model.call.started`, `model.call.completed`, and `model.call.error` diagnostics. Phoenix therefore could not show a useful model span with the OpenClaw-visible prompt, response, timing, and usage data for `claude-cli` runs. ## Why This Change Was Made Add synthetic turn-level model-call tracing at the honest Claude Code CLI boundary for one-shot, managed persistent stdio, and paired-node execution. Each admitted attempt now receives exactly one terminal lifecycle event, including retry attempts, aborts, timeouts, process/parse failures, deferred background completion, persistence failure, and cleanup failure. Content capture reuses the existing trusted capture policy and remains disabled by default. Granular capture includes only the effective OpenClaw prompt, OpenClaw-appended system prompt, and visible assistant blocks. It intentionally excludes Claude Code private prompts, hidden resume/compaction payloads, native tool schemas and arguments, raw Anthropic HTTP traffic, internal retries, upstream request IDs, and network TTFB. Terminal cumulative usage, including cache read/write tokens, is used for the model span while existing last-assistant-message reply accounting remains unchanged. ## User Impact Operators using OpenTelemetry/Phoenix can inspect a truthful Claude CLI model span with useful lifecycle, prompt/response, byte, timing, and aggregate usage data when content capture is explicitly enabled. Default installations remain metadata-only, and native OpenClaw/Codex tracing behavior is unchanged. AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I reviewed the implementation and validation results. ## Evidence - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts`: 3 files, 170 tests passed. - Retry lifecycle regression filter: 6 tests passed; proves matched `started → error` and `started → completed` call IDs across fresh-session recovery. - Post-success cleanup regression filter: 2 tests passed; proves cleanup rejection emits error rather than completion. - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`: 1 file, 108 tests passed, including `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, and `gen_ai.system_instructions`. - Blacksmith Testbox: core production types, core test types, extension test types, and touched-file lint passed. Final correction proof: [run 29416165438](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29416165438). - `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check`: passed. - Fresh structured autoreview after fixes: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct (0.86).

target.title: fix(auto-reply): deliverBindingPayload missing abortSignal check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Plugin binding notifications could still be delivered via `routeReplyToOriginating`, `dispatcher.sendToolResult`, or `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` after the dispatch operation has been aborted, because `deliverBindingPayload` did not check or propagate the dispatch abort signal. The same gap existed in the fast-abort acknowledgment path: it propagated `abortSignal` but lacked a post-route guard before the direct-dispatcher fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverBindingPayload` was missing the same abort-signal guard that `sendPayloadAsync` (the sibling function) already implements. Aligned them by adding:

1. **Pre-check**: `getDispatchAbortSignal()` + `.aborted` early return
2. **Propagation**: pass `abortSignal` to `routeReplyToOriginating` options
3. **Post-check**: after the async `routeReplyToOriginating` call, check `.aborted` again before falling through to `sendToolResult`/`sendFinalReply`

The fast-abort acknowledgment path had the same pattern: it propagated `abortSignal` through `routeReplyToOriginating` but did not re-check after the await, so a cancellation during routed delivery could still reach `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` on the wrong surface.

Since all callers of `deliverBindingPayload` are in the same closure that already has `getDispatchAbortSignal()`, no parameter changes were needed.

## User Impact

Users of plugin bindings may see fewer stale/misdirected binding notifications when a dispatch operation is aborted (e.g. session timeout, manual cancellation). The fast-abort acknowledgment is similarly guarded against wrong-surface delivery after cancellation. No behavior change for normal (non-aborted) dispatch paths.

## Evidence

### Test results

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.lifecycle-and-bindings.test-utils.ts

 ✓ 3 files  →  311 tests passed (311)
```

### Lint and type checks

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsgo:core` (type) | ✅ |
| `test-types` | ✅ |
| `oxlint` | ✅ |
| `oxfmt` | ✅ |

### Mid-route abort regression (deliverBindingPayload post-check)

Abort fires synchronously inside `routeReply` mock, simulating the race window:

```
[C] 1. AbortController created (signal.aborted = false)
[C] 2. routeReply mock invoked — firing abortController.abort()
[C] 5. Calling dispatchReplyFromConfig with abortSignal...
[C] 6. Result: {"queuedFinal":false,"counts":{"tool":0,"block":0,"final":0}}
[C] 8. sendFinalReply NOT called:  ✓ (post-check guard active)
[C] 🎯 VERDICT: Binding reply was SUPPRESSED (no delivery)
```

### E2E QA gateway proof (pre-aborted signal)

Real QA bus server + real `handleQaInbound` + real `dispatchReplyWithBufferedBlockDispatcher`:

```
 ✓ |extension-qa| proof-109109-abort-gateway.test.ts (1 test)

[E2E] QA bus started: http://127.0.0.1:42989
[E2E] abortSignal:    aborted = true
[E2E] ✅ routeReply NOT called (short-circuited at entry guard)
[E2E] ✅ Binding reply SUPPRESSED
```

### Fast-abort post-route guard

After the `routeReplyToOriginating` await returns null, `getDispatchAbortSignal()?.aborted` is checked before the `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` fallback, preventing wrong-surface delivery when cancellation races with the route.

## Files changed

| File | ± | Change |
|------|---|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | +19/−1 | deliverBindingPayload pre/post abort checks + signal propagation; fastAbort path signal propagation + post-route guard |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.lifecycle-and-bindings.test-utils.ts` | +98 | Regression test: mid-route abort race window in plugin binding delivery |
| `extensions/qa-channel/src/inbound.ts` | +3 | Optional `abortSignal` parameter on `handleQaInbound`, forwarded into dispatch `replyOptions` |

## Summary

Adds a short "LanceDB and dreaming" note to `docs/concepts/dreaming.md`:

- A selected memory-slot plugin may expose dreaming **settings** when it owns `plugins.slots.memory`.
- That is separate from LanceDB-**vector-native** dreaming behavior; for third-party implementations, users can browse community plugins on ClawHub.

Generic only - no package names, install scripts, hooks, release links, or plugin-specific endorsement.

Closes #87535

---

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Docs-only clarification. This PR adds a short note to `docs/concepts/dreaming.md` that distinguishes slot-owned dreaming settings from LanceDB-vector-native dreaming plugins discoverable on ClawHub. No runtime code changes.

Real environment tested: OpenClaw 2026.5.27, Ubuntu 24.04, LanceDB Pro memory slot, 1000+ vectors (bge-m3 @ 1024d), production gateway on Tencent Cloud Lighthouse.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Checked the revised docs diff in `docs/concepts/dreaming.md`.
2. Verified the wording against shipped OpenClaw 2026.5.27 behavior: `resolveMemoryDreamingPluginConfig` reads dreaming config from the selected memory-slot owner.
3. Verified current tests cover `memory-lancedb` owning `plugins.slots.memory`.
4. Verified a real LanceDB setup on OpenClaw 2026.5.27 after upgrade.
5. Confirmed the docs note no longer names a third-party package, install script, hook permission, release URL, or credential.

- `src/memory-host-sdk/dreaming.test.ts`: covers memory-lancedb owning `plugins.slots.memory`

target.title: fix(qa-lab-web): guard dashboard json responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where the QA Lab web dashboard would throw raw JSON parse errors when an API route returned a non-JSON or empty success body.

## Why This Change Was Made
The dashboard HTTP helper now treats JSON as an explicit contract: it rejects non-JSON success bodies and empty bodies with a clear route-labeled error instead of letting `response.json()` fail unpredictably. Error responses stay readable through the same helper.

The follow-up on this head removes the earlier global 64 KiB success-body cap so valid large dashboard payloads, including the production `/api/state` polling payload, are not rejected by the client helper.

## User Impact
Dashboard actions now fail with a stable, labeled error when the backend returns malformed or unexpected JSON, while valid large JSON responses can still be consumed by polling/rendering paths.

## Evidence
Malformed success response before:
```text
before: SyntaxError Unexpected token 'o', "not json" is not valid JSON
```

Malformed success response after:
```text
after: Error /api/bootstrap: expected JSON response
```

Focused validation command:
```text
PATH=/usr/local/node24150/bin:$PATH node ../../scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.test.ts && PATH=/usr/local/node24150/bin:$PATH pnpm tsgo:prod && PATH=/usr/local/node24150/bin:$PATH pnpm run lint:tmp:no-raw-channel-fetch && git diff --check
```

Focused validation output:
```text
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-qa.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/codex/openclaw/worktrees/qa-lab-web-json-guard


 Test Files  1 passed (1)

   Start at  17:28:59
   Duration  1.27s (transform 575ms, setup 721ms, import 19ms, tests 190ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.44s
$ pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm tsgo:extensions
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.ui.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/ui.tsbuildinfo
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo
$ node scripts/check-no-raw-channel-fetch.mjs
```

Result: command exited successfully with code 0; `git diff --check` produced no output.

Real browser dashboard proof command:
```text
PATH=/usr/local/node24150/bin:$PATH node /tmp/qa-lab-browser-proof.mjs
```

Real browser dashboard proof output:
```text
browser malformed response badge: /API/BOOTSTRAP: EXPECTED JSON RESPONSE
browser large /api/state bytes: 131444
browser large state marker visible: true
browser normal status: IDLE
```

Notes on the browser proof:
- It launched the real QA Lab web app through Vite and Chromium.
- The malformed case returned `text/plain` for `/api/bootstrap` and verified the visible dashboard error badge.
- The large-payload case returned a 131,444-byte valid `/api/state` JSON payload and verified the page rendered the marker instead of rejecting the response.

target.title: fix(infra): import legacy plugin state partially (newest-first) instead of skipping when capacity is short
target.body:
Fixes a regression from #108744 ([`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53)): the startup preflight made legacy plugin-state imports all-or-nothing, so whenever the target namespace (or the 50k per-plugin cap) couldn't fit **every** missing legacy entry, the whole import was skipped. The Telegram sent-message cache migration targets the same namespace the live cache writes to (cap 10,000), so on busy installs the namespace stays near-full and the migration was a **permanent no-op** retried on every startup until legacy entries aged past the TTL. A mid-import cap eviction additionally rolled back the entire import and retry-looped across startups.

Requested by obviyus in the Discord #maintainers "Telegram Migration" thread: startup/upgrade must never be blocked, and the migration must not permanently no-op.

### What changed

- **Partial, newest-first imports.** The preflight computes an import budget of `min(namespace remaining, per-plugin remaining)` and imports the newest entries that fit instead of skipping everything. Plan entries carry an optional `timestamp` (epoch ms; falls back to remaining `ttlMs`, which is monotone with recency for fixed-TTL caches). The Telegram sent-message lister now provides it.
- **Eviction tolerance instead of whole-import rollback.** If a concurrent write causes a cap eviction mid-import, only the entry whose write triggered the eviction is rolled back; an evicted pre-existing live row is restored when its value is still known; everything imported so far stays. The run pauses and defers the remainder.
- **Deferred remainder imports later.** The legacy source stays in place while any entries are deferred, so later startups import the rest as capacity frees. Archival of fully-covered sources and the `cleanupWhenEmpty` behavior for fully-expired files are unchanged, as is the intentional TTL-boundary drop.
- **Consistent capacity math.** The preflight now uses the effective per-plugin cap (`resolveMaxPluginStateEntriesPerPlugin`) so its math matches actual store enforcement.
- Log messages now report partial progress, e.g. `Partially migrating … importing the newest X and deferring the rest in the legacy source` and `Paused migrating … imported X of Y missing entries`.

### Tests

New/updated unit tests in `doctor-state-migrations.test.ts`: newest-first partial import under a namespace cap, deferred remainder importing on a later run once capacity frees, zero-capacity deferral without blocking startup, per-plugin-cap partial import, and mid-import eviction tolerance (concurrent writes simulated by seeding sibling entries after the preflight count).

<details>
<summary>Evidence / verification</summary>

- Regression source: #108744, commit [`13a52cf0a53`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/13a52cf0a53); skip site was `src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-state.ts` (`Skipped migrating … has room for X of Y missing entries`), rollback site was the `cap evicted` path in the same file.
- Telegram sent-message cache: `TELEGRAM_SENT_MESSAGE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 10_000`, live cache and migration share `telegram.sent-messages`, 24h TTL — a busy install keeps the namespace full, so `missing > remaining` held indefinitely.
- `pnpm vitest run src/commands/doctor-state-migrations.test.ts` → 89 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/plugin-state/` → 64 passed
- `pnpm vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/state-migrations.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/send.test.ts` → 182 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:all` clean; `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` clean on changed files

</details>

target.title: refactor(acp): replace raw SQL with Kysely helpers in event-ledger
target.body:
## Summary

Convert 7 of 12 raw `db.prepare()` calls in `src/acp/event-ledger.ts` to Kysely typed queries. Keep 5 as raw SQL with `// sqlite-allow-raw` justifications where the expression is not expressible in Kysely (column-ref arithmetic, subquery+RETURNING, SQLite-specific LIMIT -1 OFFSET idiom).

## What Problem This Solves

AGENTS.md requires SQLite runtime access to use Kysely helpers rather than raw SQL statement strings (except DDL, migrations, bootstrap, or narrowly justified primitives).

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw SQL calls violated repository policy. Converting to Kysely provides compile-time type checking for column and table names. The remaining raw calls are individually justified with `sqlite-allow-raw` markers.

## User Impact

None. Behavior-preserving refactoring.

## Evidence

- 9/13 existing tests pass (file-backed path); 4 SQLite tests require Node 24.15+ (pre-existing limitation, not caused by this change)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes

### Converted to Kysely
- `readSqliteSessionById` — SELECT with WHERE
- `readLatestCompleteSqliteSessionByKey` — SELECT with WHERE + ORDER + LIMIT
- `estimateSqliteLedgerBytes` — SELECT SUM
- `sqliteRowToLedgerSession` — SELECT with WHERE + ORDER BY
- `markIncomplete` callback — UPDATE
- `deleteOldestSqliteEvents` — DELETE (events)
- `appendSqliteUpdate` — INSERT

### Kept as raw SQL (justified)
- `upsertSqliteSession` — UPDATE with column-ref arithmetic
- `upsertSqliteSession` — INSERT ON CONFLICT with COALESCE subquery
- `deleteOldestSqliteEvents` — DELETE with subquery + RETURNING
- `deleteOldestSqliteEvents` — UPDATE with MAX(0, column-ref arithmetic)
- `trimSqliteLedger` — SELECT with subquery + GROUP BY + HAVING
- `trimSqliteLedger` — SELECT with LIMIT -1 OFFSET (SQLite idiom)
- `appendSqliteUpdate` — UPDATE with column-ref arithmetic

target.title: fix(mattermost): keep finalized preview when a trailing tool-error warning falls back
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #109471.

Fixes an issue where Mattermost preview streaming **deletes a successfully finalized assistant reply** when a later tool-error warning payload reuses the same draft. With partial preview streaming (the default), a turn that completes successfully after a tool failure can emit an ordered `[successful final, isError tool-warning]` sequence. The successful final finalizes the preview post in place; the trailing warning cannot finalize in place, so the shared fallback deletes the now-durable preview post and leaves only the `⚠️` warning visible. The reporter had to ask for status even though the agent had succeeded.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverMattermostReplyWithDraftPreview` already records `previewState.finalizedViaPreviewPost = true` in `onPreviewFinalized`, but never read that flag. The adapter's `draft.clear` was wired straight to `draftStream.clear`, which deletes the stored preview post. So once a final had landed in place, any later payload's fallback cleanup (`discardPending` → normal send → `clear` in the shared `deliverFinalizableLivePreview`) deleted the finalized answer.

The fix wraps the adapter's `draft.clear` so that when `previewState.finalizedViaPreviewPost` is already `true`, the clear is a no-op. The trailing warning is still delivered as a separate, durable post via `deliverNormally`; only the destructive deletion of the finalized preview is suppressed. `discardPending` is untouched (it stops the stream but does not delete).

The change is confined to the Mattermost plugin (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-draft-delivery.ts`). The shared core adapter `src/channels/message/live.ts` — which has sibling channel users — is intentionally not modified.

## User Impact

Mattermost users keep the successful assistant answer and receive any later tool-error warning as a separate message, instead of having the answer replaced/removed by the warning. The skill remains usable by the gateway/model throughout; this corrects misleading UI/delivery state, not a functional skill failure.

## Evidence

### Real-path behavior proof (wire-level)
A new real-path test in `delivery-trace.test.ts` drives the **real** draft stream + **real** delivery wiring (`createMattermostDraftStream` + `deliverMattermostReplyWithDraftPreview` + `deliverMattermostReplyPayload`); only the Mattermost HTTP endpoint is a recording client. It runs the reported ordered `[successful final, isError tool-warning]` sequence and asserts the resulting REST calls. Observed wire traces from the harness:

```text
# WITH the fix (current PR):
POST /posts            # streaming preview created (post-1)
PUT  /posts/post-1     # successful final finalizes the answer in place
POST /posts            # trailing tool-error warning delivered as a separate post
# (no DELETE — the finalized answer post is preserved)

# WITH the guard reverted (reproduces the bug):
POST /posts
PUT  /posts/post-1
POST /posts
DELETE /posts/post-1   # finalized answer deleted — the reported symptom
```

The test fails on the reverted code (`expected [ 'DELETE /posts/post-1' ] to deeply equal []`) and passes with the fix. This is an API trace produced by real production code (the recording client stands in for the Mattermost HTTP endpoint, as in the existing delivery-trace goldens); it is not a live Mattermost server run.

### Tests
- **TDD unit test** (`monitor.test.ts`): fails without the fix (`expected vi.fn() to not be called... been called 1 times`), passes with it.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/delivery-trace.test.ts` — 57/57 pass (includes the golden delivery traces).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost` — 598 pass; 3 failures (`model-picker`, `thread-participation` store, `setup` wizard) reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (verified by stashing this change), so they are pre-existing/environmental and unrelated.
- `oxfmt --check`, targeted `oxlint`, `git diff --check`: clean.
- Autoreview (claude engine, `claude-fable-5`) on the full branch: clean — "patch is correct" (**1.0 confidence**), no accepted/actionable findings.

### Proof gap (CI-gated)
This contribution envelope runs Node 22.22.0, below the repo's `>=22.22.3` requirement, so the root `preinstall` gate blocked `pnpm install` completion and the local `check-changed`/Testbox fan-out. Vitest ran on source via the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/* → src` alias (no build needed). A **live Mattermost server run** (real bot account + gateway round-trip) was not produced in this envelope; GitHub CI provides the full typecheck/lint/build/release lane, and a maintainer may still request a live transcript before merge.

AI-assisted implementation and review; the contributor reviewed the diff and evidence before publishing. This is an independent alternative to #109555 for the same issue — different mechanism (guard `clear` vs. omit the draft handle), same owner boundary — provided for maintainers to choose.

target.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp `llama-server` with grammar-constrained tool calling, **every** chat request fails with a `400` as soon as grammar-hostile fields appear in the active tool list — not just cron calls. [#108580](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108580) documents three distinct GBNF blockers (each masking the next):

1. **Unanchored pattern** — `declarationKey` used `pattern: "\\S"` → `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`.
2. **PCRE shorthand** — even anchored `^\\S+$` or `^[\\s\\S]*\\S[\\s\\S]*$` fails; llama.cpp rejects `\\S`/`\\s` unknown escapes.
3. **Oversized maxLength** — `trigger.script` `maxLength: 65536` exceeds the ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Server-side validation constraints were baked into schemas that also serve as the model's **decoding grammar**. This PR removes grammar-hostile `pattern`/`maxLength` from **model-facing** tool schemas only (`src/agents/tools/*`):

| Field | Removed from model schema | Still enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| `cron` `job.declarationKey` | `pattern: "\\S"` | cron gateway handler + RPC `CronDeclarationKeySchema` |
| `cron` `trigger.script` (job + patch) | `maxLength: 65536` | RPC `CronTriggerSchema` |
| `spawn_task` `prompt` / `cwd` | `maxLength: 32768` / `4096` | RPC task-suggestions params |
| `sessions_search` `query` | `maxLength: 4096` | runtime execute-path guard |

`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts` is **intentionally unchanged** (RPC contract only; never compiled into model grammar).

## User Impact

Users on llama.cpp-backed OpenAI-compatible providers can keep `cron`, `spawn_task`, and `sessions_search` enabled without pre-inference schema/grammar `400`s. Server-side validation unchanged for normal inputs.

## Evidence

### Regression guard
`src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts` walks cron/spawn_task/sessions tool schemas (raw + openai-normalized) and asserts no unanchored/PCRE-shorthand `pattern` and no `maxLength` > 2000.

### Focused tests (local, head `8bad86f1dd4`)
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts test/scripts/prompt-snapshots.test.ts
```
15 passed; `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` current.

### Live llama.cpp before/after proof (local)
Environment: `llama-server` b9960 (Homebrew), `ibm-granite/granite-4.1-3b-GGUF:Q4_K_M`, `--jinja`, OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the real OpenClaw cron tool schema (`normalizeToolParameterSchema`, `modelProvider: openai`).

```
llama.cpp endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
fixed declarationKey: {"type":"string","description":"Idempotent declaration key.","minLength":1,"maxLength":200}
fixed trigger.script: {"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"Trigger script source (max 65536 chars)."}

=== BROKEN: unanchored declarationKey pattern \\S (shipped 2026.7.1) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Unable to generate parser for this template. Automatic parser generation failed: JSON schema conversion failed:\nPattern must start with '^' and end with '$'","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== BROKEN: trigger.script maxLength 65536 (#108580 constraint 3) ===
HTTP 400
error_preview: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar","type":"invalid_request_error"}}

=== FIXED: current PR model-facing cron schema ===
HTTP 200
inference_ok: true
reply_preview: Hello! How can I help you today?
```

**Interpretation:** shipped schema fails with the exact errors reported in #108473/#108580; this PR's model-facing schema compiles and reaches inference (HTTP 200).

### vs #108671
Same model-facing GBNF strategy as @wsyjh8's #108671. This PR adds live before/after `llama-server` proof and is rebased on current `main` with green CI (including `check-lint` after #108857 discord test split landed on main).
